mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares bulk (hydrostatic) stress with shear stress in a solid material?

options.A: Bulk stress acts perpendicular to the surface and is the same in all directions, while shear stress acts parallel to the surface and varies with direction.
options.B: Bulk stress acts parallel to the surface and is direction‑dependent, whereas shear stress acts perpendicular and is isotropic.
options.C: Both bulk and shear stresses act only on the surface of a material.
options.D: Bulk stress is always larger than shear stress for any applied load.

mcqs.answer: Bulk stress acts perpendicular to the surface and is the same in all directions, while shear stress acts parallel to the surface and varies with direction.
mcqs.explanation: Bulk (hydrostatic) stress is normal to every surface element and has the same magnitude in all three orthogonal directions, representing uniform compression. Shear stress, on the other hand, acts tangentially to a surface and its magnitude depends on the direction of the applied force. Therefore option A correctly captures the comparison; the other options either reverse the definitions or make incorrect universal statements.

mcqs.question: A rectangular block of dimensions 2 cm × 4 cm × 5 cm is subjected to a force of 120 N acting parallel to its 2 cm × 5 cm face. What is the magnitude of the tangential stress on that face?
mcqs.explanation: Tangential stress = Force / Area. The area of the 2 cm × 5 cm face is 10 cm² = 1 × 10⁻³ m². Stress = 120 N / 1 × 10⁻³ m² = 1.2 × 10⁵ N/m² = 120 kPa. Options A, B, and D result from incorrect area conversion or arithmetic errors.

mcqs.question: In the context of solid mechanics, stress is best defined as:

options.A: The force applied per unit volume of a material.
options.B: The internal restoring force per unit area within a material.
options.C: The displacement of a material per unit length.
options.D: The energy stored per unit mass of a material.

mcqs.answer: The internal restoring force per unit area within a material.
mcqs.explanation: Stress quantifies how internal forces are distributed over a material's internal area. It is not related to volume (option A), displacement (option C), or energy per mass (option D). Hence option B is the precise definition.

mcqs.question: A steel rod with a cross‑sectional area of 8 mm² is pulled by a force of 400 N. What is the normal stress in the rod?
mcqs.explanation: Convert area: 8 mm² = 8 × 10⁻⁶ m². Stress = Force / Area = 400 N / 8 × 10⁻⁶ m² = 5 × 10⁷ N/m² = 50 MPa. Options A, C, and D arise from misplaced decimal points.

mcqs.question: Longitudinal stress in a rod differs from bulk stress in that:

options.A: Longitudinal stress acts uniformly in all directions, while bulk stress acts only along the length of the rod.
options.B: Longitudinal stress is normal to the cross‑section and acts along the length, whereas bulk stress is hydrostatic and acts equally in all three dimensions.
options.C: Longitudinal stress is a shear stress, while bulk stress is a normal stress.
options.D: Longitudinal stress only occurs in fluids, while bulk stress occurs only in solids.

mcqs.answer: Longitudinal stress is normal to the cross‑section and acts along the length, whereas bulk stress is hydrostatic and acts equally in all three dimensions.
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal (or normal) stress is directed along the axis of a member, perpendicular to its cross‑section. Bulk (hydrostatic) stress is isotropic, acting equally in all directions within a material. Options A, C, and D misrepresent the nature of these stresses.

mcqs.question: A cubic block of metal is placed at a depth of 30 m under water (density of water = 1000 kg/m³). Assuming atmospheric pressure is 1 × 10⁵ Pa, what is the bulk stress acting uniformly throughout the block?
mcqs.explanation: Pressure at depth = ρgh + atmospheric pressure = 1000 kg/m³ × 9.8 m/s² × 30 m + 1 × 10⁵ Pa = 2.94 × 10⁵ Pa + 1 × 10⁵ Pa ≈ 3.94 × 10⁵ Pa, which rounds to 3.9 × 10⁵ Pa. This pressure is hydrostatic, i.e., bulk stress, acting equally in all directions. Options A and B ignore water pressure; D overestimates.

mcqs.question: A block of wood of mass 10 kg rests on a rough horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is 0.4 and the contact area is 0.05 m². What is the maximum tangential stress the contact surface can sustain before the block starts sliding?
mcqs.explanation: Maximum static friction force = μ mg = 0.4 × 10 kg × 9.8 m/s² = 39.2 N. Tangential stress = force / area = 39.2 N / 0.05 m² = 784 Pa. Option B is correct; the others result from incorrect division or unit conversion.

mcqs.question: A metal rod of length 1 m and cross‑sectional area 2 mm² is pulled by a force of 600 N. In this scenario, which statement correctly defines the stress experienced by the rod?

options.A: Stress is the total force applied to the rod, i.e., 600 N.
options.B: Stress is the force per unit length of the rod.
options.C: Stress is the internal restoring force per unit area, calculated as 600 N divided by 2 mm².
options.D: Stress is the deformation (extension) of the rod per unit length.

mcqs.answer: Stress is the internal restoring force per unit area, calculated as 600 N divided by 2 mm².
mcqs.explanation: Stress is defined as force per unit area. Here the area is 2 mm², so stress = 600 N / 2 mm². Options A and B misinterpret the definition, and D describes strain, not stress. Hence option C is correct.
